chapter_name: Chapter 04: Nouns, Pronouns, and Their Features
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will understand advanced features of nouns, including cases and apposition, and master complex pronouns like relative, reflexive, and emphatic pronouns.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Nouns and Pronouns are the main characters of our sentences. But just like actors in a movie, they change their roles, cases, and costumes depending on the scene! Let's explore their advanced features. 🎭

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A noun's 'Case' shows its role. It can be Nominative (Subject), Objective (Object), or Possessive (Owner). 'Apposition' happens when two nouns are placed side-by-side to describe the exact same person or thing.
examples_or_templates: Case: The dog (Nominative) bit the postman (Objective).
Apposition: Mr. Sharma, our principal, gave a speech. ('our principal' is in apposition to 'Mr. Sharma')

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Both end in '-self' or '-selves' (myself, herself). A Reflexive pronoun acts as the object when the subject and object are the same person. An Emphatic pronoun is just used to put heavy emphasis on the subject and can be removed without ruining the sentence.
examples_or_templates: Reflexive: He cut himself. (Subject 'He' = Object 'himself'. Cannot remove it!)
Emphatic: I myself baked this cake. (Emphasis. You can say 'I baked this cake' and it still makes sense.)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Relative pronouns (who, whom, whose, which, that) connect a dependent clause to a main clause. They refer back to a noun mentioned previously, which is called the 'Antecedent'.
examples_or_templates: The man WHO is wearing a red shirt is my uncle. ('Who' relates back to the antecedent 'man'.)
This is the book THAT I borrowed. ('That' relates to 'book'.)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the phrase in apposition: 'My best friend, a talented artist, painted this portrait.'
❓ Is the highlighted word Reflexive or Emphatic? 'The Queen HERSELF awarded the medal.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Combine these sentences using a relative pronoun: 'Here is the watch. You lost it yesterday.'
✍️ Identify the noun in the Objective Case: 'The fierce lion chased the frightened deer.'
subjective_practice.hint: Who or what received the action of the verb 'chased'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with a reflexive pronoun: 'They accidentally locked _______ out of the house.'
subjective_practice.hint: It needs to match the subject 'They'.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🤝 The Apposition Introductions
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write 3 sentences introducing your family members or friends using Nouns in Apposition. Example: 'My brother, a giant dinosaur fan, is reading a book.' Don't forget the commas!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Nouns change 'Case' based on if they are the subject, object, or owner.
⭐ Nouns in Apposition are placed side-by-side to describe the same person.
⭐ Reflexive pronouns receive the action (can't be removed); Emphatic pronouns just add emphasis (can be removed).
⭐ Relative pronouns (who, which, that) connect clauses and refer back to an antecedent.
